Write a corpus in theoryforge's corpus schema

Source: R/corpus.R
write_scopus_corpus.Rd

Turns a scopus_corpus() result into the literature corpus that theoryforge's tf_read_corpus(), tf_litmap() and tf_landscape() read, following the corpus schema theoryforge publishes (schema/corpus.schema.json in its repository). as_theoryforge_corpus() returns the document as a list, and write_scopus_corpus() writes it to a JSON file. Neither needs theoryforge installed, and neither makes a request.

Usage

as_theoryforge_corpus(corpus, id)

write_scopus_corpus(corpus, path, id)

Arguments

corpus

A scopus_corpus() result, or a data frame with the same id, title, year, keywords and references columns, where each references entry is a data frame with id and doi columns. A scopus_id column is used when present.

id

A non-empty string naming the corpus, written as its top-level id. It is required, since a scopus_corpus() result carries no name of its own.

path

The file to write, exactly as given. Parent directories are assumed to exist already.

Value

as_theoryforge_corpus() returns the document as a list with the elements id, provenance, records and schema_version ("1.0"). write_scopus_corpus() returns the same list invisibly.

Details

theoryforge compares references as exact strings, so the writer gives each cited work one key across the whole corpus, its 'Scopus' identifier, as scopus:<id>. 'Scopus' gives a cited work's DOI in some bibliographies only, and in different cases. A key built from the DOI wherever there is one would therefore split one work into several nodes and lose the co-citation edges between them. A reference that carries only a DOI takes the 'Scopus' identifier that a document or reference elsewhere in the corpus pairs with the same DOI, the documents' own identifiers counting first. A DOI that nothing pairs with is keyed as doi:<doi>, without its resolver prefix and with its ASCII letters lower-cased, since DOIs are case-insensitive over ASCII (DOI Handbook, section 2.4). A reference with neither is dropped, and a scopus_warning_dropped_references warning says how many. Each document is keyed the same way, from its scopus_id or else from an id that is a DOI or a 'Scopus' identifier, so a citation of a document in the corpus and the document itself share one key.

Keywords are trimmed, lower-cased with tolower() and made unique, keeping the first of each, and empty ones are dropped, so "Graphene" and "graphene " count as one keyword. The Python twin lower-cases with str.lower(). The two agree on the Latin, Greek and Cyrillic letters in common use and differ on a few special cases, such as the Turkish capital I with a dot and a capital sigma ending a word, which Python writes as a final sigma. A missing year is written as null, and a missing title is left out, since the schema admits the one and not the other.

The document also carries a provenance object, which the schema admits beside its own fields: source ("Scopus via scopusflow <version>"), query, retrieved_at (in UTC, as YYYY-MM-DDTHH:MM:SSZ), keywords, n_records, n_references_dropped and n_records_without_keywords. query, retrieved_at and keywords come from the attributes scopus_corpus() attaches, and are null when the corpus lacks them. query is a string, or an array of strings when the records were searched with several expressions. Author keywords can come back empty under some entitlements (see scopus_abstract()), which leaves theoryforge's keyword themes empty whatever the writer does, and n_records_without_keywords shows when that happened.

The file is UTF-8, with no escaping beyond what JSON requires, sorted keys, no spaces between tokens and one line feed at the end, so the same corpus gives the same bytes from either twin.

See also

scopus_corpus(), which builds the corpus.

Examples

# Two records of the bundled corpus of real articles, each citing the same
# two others. The keywords and the citations are illustrative, since the
# bundled records carry neither.
docs <- example_records[!is.na(example_records$doi), ][1:4, ]
cited <- tibble::tibble(id = NA_character_, doi = docs$doi[3:4])
corpus <- tibble::tibble(
  id = docs$doi[1:2],
  scopus_id = NA_character_,
  title = docs$title[1:2],
  year = docs$year[1:2],
  keywords = list(c("Graphene", "supercapacitor"), "graphene"),
  references = list(cited, cited)
)
doc <- as_theoryforge_corpus(corpus, id = "graphene-supercapacitors")
doc$records[[1]]$keywords
#> [1] "graphene"       "supercapacitor"
doc$records[[1]]$references
#> [1] "doi:10.1016/j.electacta.2015.02.019" "doi:10.1002/smll.201403383"         

# Written to a temporary file (never the working directory).
path <- tempfile(fileext = ".json")
write_scopus_corpus(corpus, path, id = "graphene-supercapacitors")
substr(readLines(path, encoding = "UTF-8"), 1, 160)
#> [1] "{\"id\":\"graphene-supercapacitors\",\"provenance\":{\"keywords\":null,\"n_records\":2,\"n_records_without_keywords\":0,\"n_references_dropped\":0,\"query\":null,\"retrieved_at\""
